input.rationale: Baseline map: one or two plain-noun prompts per KITTI class, with synonyms for car, truck, pedestrian, and cyclist, and a single tram prompt, to see which classes the detector responds to before refining.

content.text: The baseline reaches mAP 0.22. Cyclist is nearly zero (AP 0.012), and "person riding a bicycle" produced 723 false positives with only 14 hits. Next I'll change only the cyclist prompts to test whether "bicycle"-centred wording works better.

input.rationale: Cyclist is the weakest class, so I'm swapping the awkward "person riding a bicycle" prompt for shorter bicycle-centred phrases ("bicycle", "bike rider") to see if they match the rider+bike box better with fewer false positives.

content.text: Bicycle-only prompts hit empty bikes, so the detector does not link the rider to the bike that way. Cyclist AP fell further to 0.002. Next I'll try rider-centred phrases that name the person.

input.rationale: Bicycle-only prompts latch onto empty parked bikes, so I'm testing rider-centred phrases ("man riding bicycle", "person on bike") to tie the detection to a person plus bike, keeping everything else fixed.

content.text: Cyclist AP is stuck near 0.01 with every rider phrasing so far. I'll set cyclist aside for now and test car and pedestrian, since the missed ground-truth cars are large nearby vans. I'm adding van-style and person-style synonyms, with cyclist back on the original prompts.

input.rationale: Car and pedestrian have the most ground truth and room to improve, so I'm adding vehicle synonyms (white van, suv) and a standing-person prompt, while restoring the original cyclist prompts to isolate the effect on car and pedestrian.

content.text: Car and pedestrian both improved slightly. "suv" and "person standing" are precise (few false positives), while "white van" and "person walking" add noise. Next I'll drop those two noisy prompts and try a plain "person" prompt for pedestrians.

input.rationale: Pruning the noisy "white van" and "person walking" prompts while keeping the precise "suv" and "person standing", and adding a plain "person" prompt for pedestrians, to raise precision and recall for pedestrians.

content.text: The best mAP so far is 0.2246. Cyclist is still near 0.01, so I'll try different cyclist wording ("bicyclist", "bike with rider") and, for trucks, add "lorry" and "box truck", which are different classes so their effects can be read separately.

input.rationale: Cyclist AP is still about 0.01, so I'm trying "bicyclist" and "bike with rider" in place of the earlier cyclist prompts, and adding "lorry" and "box truck" to see whether truck recall improves.

content.text: Adding "lorry" helped trucks (8 correct, only 4 false positives), but the new cyclist wording was worse, so I'll revert cyclist to the earlier prompts. For trams I'll add "streetcar" and "light rail", since the tram prompt is the only one that fires there.

input.rationale: Combining the gains so far (suv, person standing, person, lorry, delivery truck) with the original cyclist prompts, and adding "streetcar" and "light rail train" to improve tram recall.

content.text: Tram AP dropped (0.236 to 0.224). Because NMS merges boxes across prompts of a class, the extra tram prompts appear to have displaced the stronger "tram" boxes. I'll revert tram to the single "tram" prompt and keep the other gains, as a final check.

input.rationale: Reverting tram to the single "tram" prompt, since the extra tram prompts reduced tram AP through NMS interactions, while keeping the car, truck and pedestrian gains.

content.text:
The best map so far scores mAP 0.225 on the development split, up from 0.220 for the baseline. I've stopped at 7 of the 15 allowed evaluation calls.

**Best prompt map (0.2253 mAP):**
- **car:** "car", "van", "suv"
- **truck:** "truck", "delivery truck", "lorry"
- **pedestrian:** "pedestrian", "person standing", "person"
- **cyclist:** "cyclist", "person riding a bicycle"
- **tram:** "tram"

**Per-class AP:**

| Class | AP | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| car | 0.379 | Strongest class; "suv" is precise (93 hits, 7 false positives) |
| truck | 0.291 | "lorry" is precise (8 hits, 4 false positives) |
| pedestrian | 0.210 | "person standing" and "person" help a little |
| tram | 0.236 | Extra tram synonyms hurt, so only "tram" is kept |
| cyclist | 0.011 | Still the main weakness |

**What I learned:**
- Cyclist barely moves whatever wording I try. Bicycle-only prompts fire on parked bikes, and rider phrasings give many false positives with few hits. The 130 cyclist ground-truth boxes are essentially unrecovered.
- Precise, specific synonyms ("suv", "lorry", "person standing") helped more than generic ones. Broad or noisy prompts ("white van", "person walking", "bicycle") lowered precision.
- Because NMS merges boxes across prompts of the same class, adding prompts can displace stronger boxes. The tram AP fell when I added "streetcar" and "light rail train".

**Next steps I'd try if continuing:** test a few more cyclist phrasings that describe the whole rider-and-bike silhouette, and check whether a large-vehicle phrase recovers the nearby vans the detector currently misses.

input.rationale: Cyclist is the weakest class, so I'm testing two more rider-plus-bike phrasings ("rider on bicycle", "person on bicycle") alongside "cyclist", holding all other classes fixed to isolate the cyclist effect.
Control run with the best map so far, included to check run-to-run stability before further cyclist changes.

content.text:
I ran two evaluations in parallel: a cyclist variant and a control. The control reproduced the earlier best score exactly (0.2253), so the evaluation is deterministic.

**Cyclist variant (best so far, mAP 0.2267):** cyclist prompts are "cyclist", "rider on bicycle", and "person on bicycle". Cyclist AP rose from 0.011 to 0.015, and the other classes are unchanged. The gain is small. "person on bicycle" produces about 800 false positives for 25 hits, so the cyclist prompts still need work.

**Control (mAP 0.2253):** same as the previous best, with cyclist prompts "cyclist" and "person riding a bicycle".

I've used 9 of 15 calls. The best map is now:
- **car:** car, van, suv
- **truck:** truck, delivery truck, lorry
- **pedestrian:** pedestrian, person standing, person
- **cyclist:** cyclist, rider on bicycle, person on bicycle
- **tram:** tram

Cyclist is still the weak point, and I don't have a phrasing that makes it work. If you want me to keep going, I'd next try a rider-only phrase (for example "bicyclist riding") or drop the cyclist prompts that generate the most false positives, and check whether the cyclist AP moves.

input.rationale: Cyclist remains the weakest class, so I'm replacing "person on bicycle" (about 800 false positives for 25 hits) with "bicyclist riding", keeping "cyclist" and "rider on bicycle", and holding the other classes fixed.

content.text:
I tried "bicyclist riding" in place of "person on bicycle" and the result is worse. Overall mAP fell to 0.2252 from the best 0.2267, and cyclist AP dropped to 0.009.

- **Cyclist:** the new prompt produced 790 false positives for 9 hits, so it's noisy. The "cyclist" prompt alone gives 15 hits, and "rider on bicycle" gives 4.
- **Pedestrian:** slightly better (0.211 vs 0.212 before, within noise), with "person" and "person standing" still contributing.
- **Other classes:** unchanged.

The best map is still the previous one (mAP 0.2267), with cyclist prompts "cyclist", "rider on bicycle", and "person on bicycle". I've used 10 of 15 calls.

Cyclist AP has stayed between 0.009 and 0.015 across every phrasing I've tried. Each cyclist phrase either finds few riders or produces hundreds of false positives on bikes or pedestrians. The next step would be a stricter cyclist-only test, but I don't expect much from it. If you'd rather stop here, the 0.2267 map is the one to keep.

input.rationale: "person on bicycle" produced about 800 false positives, so I'm dropping it and keeping only "cyclist" and "rider on bicycle" for cyclists, to see whether cutting that noise improves the cyclist AP.

content.text:
Dropping "person on bicycle" gave mAP 0.2259, a little below the best 0.2267. Cyclist AP rose slightly to 0.0125 (from 0.0107 on the older cyclist set and 0.0151 on the best set), but that is still very low. The false positives fell from about 800 to 27 for "rider on bicycle", while "cyclist" produced 650 false positives for 21 hits.

Tram is unchanged at 0.236, and car, truck and pedestrian are stable. The best map is still the one from the cyclist variant (mAP 0.2267), which keeps "person on bicycle". The difference is small enough to be within the noise of these per-class estimates.

I've used 11 of 15 calls. Cyclist remains essentially unsolved: no phrasing I've tried gets much above 0.015 AP without a flood of false positives. I'd recommend keeping the 0.2267 map, and I can use the remaining calls on a tighter cyclist test or stop here.

input.rationale: Testing whether adding "person riding a bicycle" to the best cyclist set (cyclist, rider on bicycle, person on bicycle) raises cyclist recall, keeping every other class fixed so any change is attributable to cyclist.

content.text:
Adding "person riding a bicycle" gave mAP 0.2265, essentially tied with the best (0.2267). Cyclist AP was 0.0146 against 0.0151, and it added about 394 false positives for 6 hits, so I'm not keeping it.

I've used 12 of 15 calls. The last several cyclist variants all land between 0.009 and 0.015 AP, and no phrasing has broken out of that range. I'm going to stop here and recommend the best map found:

- **car:** car, van, suv
- **truck:** truck, delivery truck, lorry
- **pedestrian:** pedestrian, person standing, person
- **cyclist:** cyclist, rider on bicycle, person on bicycle
- **tram:** tram

That map scores mAP 0.2267 (car 0.379, truck 0.291, pedestrian 0.212, cyclist 0.015, tram 0.236). The remaining 3 calls would most likely produce only marginal changes, so I'd rather not spend them. If you want to push further, the next thing to test is whether cyclist AP responds to any change in the image-side prompt, which is outside what this prompt-map setup can control.

input.rationale: Car is the class with the most ground truth, so I'm adding "minivan" to the best map to test whether it recovers more of the large vans the detector currently misses, keeping all other classes fixed.

content.text:
Adding "minivan" to the car class gives a new best mAP of **0.2281**, up from 0.2267. Car AP rose from 0.379 to 0.386, and the other classes are unchanged.

"minivan" is the most precise car prompt so far: 174 correct detections and 11 false positives. Some of its matches may overlap with "van" and "suv" boxes, which NMS merges, so the gain comes from covering vehicles the other prompts miss rather than from new boxes alone.

Current best map:
- **car:** car, van, suv, minivan
- **truck:** truck, delivery truck, lorry
- **pedestrian:** pedestrian, person standing, person
- **cyclist:** cyclist, rider on bicycle, person on bicycle
- **tram:** tram

I've used 13 of 15 calls. Cyclist is still the weak class (AP 0.015), and I don't have a phrasing that improves it without adding many false positives. I'd suggest keeping this map as the final unless you want me to spend the last two calls on another car or truck synonym.

input.rationale: Truck is the other class with a small ground-truth count where a single extra synonym could move AP, so I'm adding "cargo truck" to the new best map and holding everything else fixed.
